title: Starting a deep trace through the API: the read chain, the request body, and where the clients disagree
aliases: start a diagnostics session via api
how many deep traces at once

prose.text: A deep trace is started with one POST per device, and the request names an application and two probes that must be read first. The endpoint and the SDK functions are generated (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface zdx`); this subject holds the body and its pitfalls.

prose.label: Reading the IDs first.
prose.text: {{read-chain}} {{probe-id-key}} Whether a probe ID read for one device and application is rejected when sent for another is open {{gap:probe-id-portability}}.

prose.label: The body the contract defines.
prose.text: {{contract-request}} {{contract-response}} The earlier questions about the session-name key and about concurrent sessions are closed {{gap:session-name-key}} {{gap:concurrent-sessions}}.

prose.label: What the clients send.
prose.text: {{python-body-passthrough}} {{go-payload}} {{go-payload-sends-all}} The cloud-path probe key differs {{divergence:cloudpath-key}}. {{python-id-types}} The Python docstring and the contract disagree on the ID type {{divergence:id-types}}.

prose.label: Session length.
prose.text: {{sdk-session-lengths}} The contract describes a shorter maximum {{divergence:session-length-range}}. {{postman-start-body}} The collection's example uses another key {{divergence:postman-length-key}}.

prose.label: What comes back.
prose.text: {{python-start-result}} {{python-start-loses-trace-id}} The Go start result is in [[zdx.sdk-go.service-defects:go-trace-id-string]]; reading the session afterwards is in [[zdx.diagnostics.session-records]].

checks.do: Whether the device already has an active deep trace, and how many are active across the tenant, including sessions started from the console.
Whether the web and cloud-path probe IDs were read for this same device and application, and taken from the probe record's `id`.
Which client built the body: a Go-built body carries `cloud_path_probe_id`, which the contract does not define.
Whether the requested session length is within the contract's stated maximum.
Where the trace ID came from: the Python start result does not carry it, so list the device's traces to find it.

session-limits.statement: The contract limits deep traces to one active session per device at any time and 15 active sessions across all devices, counting sessions started from the UI.

expect.description: Start deep trace on a device. Limited to 1 active session on a device at any time. Overall 15 active sessions at any point of time across all devices - includes sessions initiated from UI.

read-chain.statement: The MCP start tool tells callers to resolve `app_id`, `web_probe_id` and `cloudpath_probe_id` with `zdx_list_applications`, `zdx_get_web_probes` and `zdx_list_cloudpath_probes` first, and the Go SDK's start example asks for the device, application, web probe and cloud-path probe IDs in that order before calling `CreateDeepTraceSession`.

quotes: createdSession, resp, err := deeptrace.CreateDeepTraceSession(ctx, service, deviceID, payload)

probe-id-key.statement: The probe records the web-probe and cloud-path-probe reads return carry the probe's ID under `id`, which the caller must pass on under the start request's `web_probe_id` or `cloudpath_probe_id` key.

quotes: self.id = config["id"] if "id" in config else None
self.id = config["id"] if "id" in config else None

probe-id-key.conditions: Rests on the Python probe models reading `id` and on the start body's key names; no source states the hand-over in one place.

contract-request.statement: The contract's start body carries `session_name` (a string), `app_id`, `web_probe_id` and `cloudpath_probe_id` (int64 integers), `session_length_minutes` (an integer described as the session length in minutes, up to 15) and `probe_device` (a boolean for device-level stats).

probe_device.description: probe device for device level stats

session_name.description: Name of the deep tracing session

contract-response.statement: A started trace answers 201 or 202 with `trace_id` (an int64 integer), `status` (one of `not_started`, `in_progress`, `error` and `done`) and `expected_time`, described as the expected completion time in epoch seconds.

expected_time.description: expected time of completion in epoch seconds
expected time of completion in epoch seconds

python-body-passthrough.statement: The Python `start_deeptrace` sends its keyword arguments as the request body (`body = kwargs`), and the request executor leaves ZDX bodies in snake_case on both the OneAPI and the legacy client, so the keys go out as passed; its docstring names the probe keyword `cloudpath_probe_id`.

quotes: cloudpath_probe_id (str): The unique ID for the Cloudpath probe.
# Ensure ZDX remains snake_case without affecting other services
if self.use_legacy_client and self.zdx_legacy_client: return body  # Do not convert anything, just return as-is # Ensure ZTB remains snake_case
return body  # Do not convert ZDX requests to camelCase

go-payload.statement: The Go SDK's `DeepTraceSessionPayload` serializes `session_name`, `app_id`, `web_probe_id`, `cloud_path_probe_id`, `session_length_minutes` and `probe_device`, with the three IDs and the length typed as Go `int`.

python-id-types.statement: The Python `start_deeptrace` docstring types `app_id`, `web_probe_id` and `cloudpath_probe_id` as `str`.

quotes: app_id (str): The unique ID for the application.
web_probe_id (str): The unique ID for the Web probe.
cloudpath_probe_id (str): The unique ID for the Cloudpath probe.

sdk-session-lengths.statement: The Python SDK docstring and the MCP start tool describe `session_length_minutes` as defaulting to 5 minutes with supported values 5, 15, 30 and 60.

quotes: session_length_minutes (int): The duration of the deeptrace session in minutes. Defaults to 5.
Field(default=5, description="Session duration in minutes. Supported: 5, 15, 30, 60."),

python-start-result.statement: The Python `start_deeptrace` builds its result as a `TraceDetails`, which reads only `session_name`, `user_id`, `username`, `device_id`, `device_name`, `session_length_minutes` and `probe_device` from the response; it has no trace ID or status attribute.

quotes: self.session_name = config["session_name"] if "session_name" in config else None
self.user_id = config["user_id"] if "user_id" in config else None
self.username = config["username"] if "username" in config else None
self.device_id = config["device_id"] if "device_id" in config else None
self.device_name = config["device_name"] if "device_name" in config else None
self.session_length_minutes = config["session_length_minutes"] if "session_length_minutes" in config else None
self.probe_device = config["probe_device"] if "probe_device" in config else None
def __init__(self, config: Optional[Any] = None) -> None: pass

python-start-result.conditions: The seven quoted assignments are every attribute the `TraceDetails` constructor sets at the pin.

python-start-loses-trace-id.statement: So the object the Python `start_deeptrace` returns does not carry the `trace_id` or `status` the contract's start response holds; the caller has to find the new trace by listing the device's traces.
python-start-loses-trace-id.conditions: Follows from the model's attribute list against the contract's response fields; not observed against a live tenant.

go-payload-sends-all.statement: None of the payload's fields is tagged `omitempty`, so a Go-built start body always carries all six keys, including a zero `session_length_minutes` and `probe_device` false when the caller leaves them unset.
go-payload-sends-all.conditions: Follows from Go's encoding/json writing every field that lacks `omitempty`; not observed on the wire.

postman-start-body.statement: The OneAPI Postman collection's `POST {{ZDXBaseUrl}}/devices/{{deviceID}}/deeptraces` request (described as "Start deep trace") sends a body with `session_name`, `app_id`, `web_probe_id`, `cloudpath_probe_id`, `session_length` (300 in the example), `probe_device` and `callback_url`.

cloudpath-key.summary: The key for the cloud-path probe in the start body: the contract and the Python and MCP callers use `cloudpath_probe_id`; the Go payload struct sends `cloud_path_probe_id`.

positions.says: The start body's cloud-path probe key is `cloudpath_probe_id`.
The Go SDK serializes the cloud-path probe ID as `cloud_path_probe_id`.

cloudpath-key.impact: A Go-built start request carries a key the contract does not define, so the cloud-path probe the caller chose may not reach the server; whether the API rejects the request, ignores the key or accepts it is not stated by any source.

id-types.summary: The type of the start body's application and probe IDs: the contract defines int64 integers; the Python docstring documents strings.

quotes: app_id (str): The unique ID for the application.

positions.says: The Python docstring types the IDs as `str`; the method sends whatever type the caller passes.

id-types.impact: A Python caller following the docstring sends the IDs as JSON strings where the contract expects integers; the MCP tool converts them to integers before calling the SDK ([[zdx.diagnostics.mcp-tools:start-tool-coerces]]).

session-length-range.summary: The allowed session length: the contract describes up to 15 minutes; the Python docstring and the MCP tool list 5, 15, 30 and 60.
session-length-range.impact: A 30- or 60-minute request that the SDK documents as supported may be refused or shortened by the API; no source shows which.

postman-length-key.summary: The start body's session-length key: the contract defines `session_length_minutes` and no callback; the Postman example sends `session_length` and a `callback_url`.

positions.says: The length key is `session_length_minutes`; the body has no `callback_url`.
The Postman start body sends `session_length` and `callback_url`.

postman-length-key.impact: A request copied from the collection carries a length key the contract does not define, and its example value of 300 is out of the contract's range if read as minutes; no source says whether the API reads `session_length`, in which unit, or what it does with `callback_url`.

probe-id-portability.title: What the API does with a probe ID read for a different device or application
probe-id-portability.detail: Unverified legacy statement: web and cloud-path probe IDs are not portable across devices or applications, because both probe reads are nested under the device and the application. The nesting is in the paths; no source states a validation rule, and the API's answer to a mismatched probe ID (an error, an empty result or a cross-match) is not stated.
probe-id-portability.blocks: telling a caller whether a probe ID can be reused across devices or applications

session-name-key.title: Which key the start request uses for the session name
session-name-key.resolution: The contract's start body names it `session_name` (claim contract-request), which both SDKs send; the Python model's mapping of the session name to `name` is not used to build the start body (claim python-body-passthrough).

concurrent-sessions.title: How many deep-trace sessions may run at once, per tenant and per device
concurrent-sessions.resolution: The contract limits deep traces to one active session per device and 15 active sessions across all devices, UI sessions included (claim session-limits).
